org: Orange (Orange Design System / Orange Unified Design System, ODS Charts)
accessNotes: The original data-display URL (37a8d3) redirects to the Zeroheight cover page; the current guide lives at 210591-data-display and its sub-pages, which are JS-rendered. Read them through a headless browser (all sub-pages: getting started, chart types, bar, line, pie/donut, gauges, colour, axes & labels, legends, data formats). The colour page renders the single/categorical/sequential swatches as images without hex; those hex values were taken from the ODS Charts (Apache ECharts theme) source on GitHub, file _ouds-colors-css-variables.ts (OUDS tokens, light and dark). The Zeroheight colour page lists functional/highlight/neutral/gridline hex values directly; ODS Charts uses slightly different hex for some (noted).
summary: Orange's data display guideline is a product-UI design-system guide for charts in Orange web/mobile apps and dashboards, implemented as ODS Charts, an Apache ECharts theme. The look is plain and Swiss: Helvetica Neue, black axis labels, light grey (#cccccc) gridlines only along the value axis, no tick marks, flat square-cornered bars, and a 10-colour categorical palette led by deep purple, green and magenta. One orange (#f16e00) is used only as a highlight colour against a neutral grey. Every colour is a design token with a light-mode and a dark-mode value.

colors.categoricalNotes: OUDS categorical tokens --ouds-charts-color-categorical-tier-1..10 (light mode), from ODS Charts source. Guide: 'The sequence is carefully curated to maximise contrast between neighbouring colours ... Colours should be applied in sequence as numbered in the token names.' All meet WCAG 2.2 AA 3:1 against the primary background in light and dark. Dark-mode tiers 1-10: #a885d8, #50be87, #ff80d4, #d6aa00, #79c7ec, #8d60cd, #9bdaba, #ff4dc3, #ffd266, #1fa2e0. The 'single' palette (for charts that do not need colour to separate categories) is tiers 1, 6, 7, 2, 5, 10 (#5b2f98, #8d60cd, #2e7b54, #3ba06e, #0073b2, #009bf0); the guide's single-series examples use #8d60cd-like violet. The legacy ODS (pre-OUDS) categorical palette was #085ebd, #27a971, #bc4d9a, #9373bd, #9d6e06, #333333, #3e9dd6, #0a6e31, #d573bb, #492191, #b98f11, #666666.
colors.notes: Sequential: five single-hue palettes (accent-1 blue shown above, tints 100-900; accent-2 green #e5f5ed..#123021, accent-3 pink #ffe5f6..#4d0033, accent-4 purple #f1ecf9..#150b23, accent-5 yellow #fff0cc..#332400). 'In light mode, lower values are lighter and higher values are darker. In Dark mode, lower values are darker and higher values are lighter.' Functional (Zeroheight page): information #4170d8, positive #228722, warning #8f7200, negative #cd3c14 — green success, blue info, yellow warning, red critical. ODS Charts OUDS tokens give positive #17a02f, warning #a38200, negative #db0002, info #009bf0. Highlight #f16e00 (Zeroheight) / #f15e00 (OUDS token light) / #ff7900 (dark), always paired with neutral #666666 (Zeroheight) / #8f8f8f (OUDS token). Gridlines and gauge 'track' are grey #cccccc (dark mode #666666). Dark backgrounds are #141414 or #000000; segment borders are #ffffff in light mode and #141414 in dark.

typography.notes: ODS Charts uses fontSize 14, weight 400 for gauge/legend labels and 40px bold for the big gauge value; the donut centre value appears on hover at 35px weight 700, formatted '{d}%'. Legend labels are 14px/16px, weight 400. Titles and subtitles always use sentence case.

structure.gridlines: Light grey #cccccc solid hairlines along the value axis only: horizontal for vertical bars and lines, vertical for horizontal bars. No gridlines along the category axis.
structure.axisLine: The category/baseline axis line is drawn in the gridline grey (#cccccc), slightly heavier than the gridlines (about 2px in the examples). ODS Charts sets axisLine show:true for every axis type.
structure.ticks: None (axisTick show:false). The line-chart example shows short grey ticks under month labels.
structure.zeroLine: The baseline at 0 is drawn as the heavier grey axis line.
structure.yAxisTitle: omitted in examples; the title describes the measure
structure.unitPlacement: In the title/subtitle; data formats put a space before % and € (e.g. '20 %', '29,99 €').
structure.background: white (#ffffff) in light mode, #141414 or #000000 in dark mode
structure.notes: Y-axis labels are right-aligned and vertically centred on the gridlines. X-axis labels are centred under bars and points. 'Always include an additional increment greater than the dataset' — the axis extends one step above the maximum.

legend.placement: Below the chart, left-aligned with the plot, is the default example. The guide also allows: left-aligned to the y-axis gridlines and the chart title; centred on the chart; left-aligned to the title and the y-axis labels; below the chart title; on top of the gridlines; above the chart title.
legend.directLabels: Not discussed; tooltips can stand in for a legend on hover.
legend.title: not shown
legend.swatchShape: square (12×12px) with a black or white outline, depending on the background
legend.notes: Use a legend only when the chart has more than one colour. Show up to two lines of legend items by default. ODS Charts renders the legend as external HTML; clicking an item toggles its series, and toggled-off items drop to 0.25 opacity.

marks.bars: Flat, square corners, no outline. In the examples the bar is about 55-60% of the band. Stacked segments are separated by thin white gaps. Horizontal bars when category labels are long. Gauge bar width 32px.
marks.lines: 2px solid. The default ODS Charts line style is SMOOTH, with options broken (straight segments, symbolSize 0), points, or none. The guide's line example is straight with no markers.
marks.points: Bubble charts are supported. Point style is not specified.
marks.pies: Allowed (pie and donut). The example starts at 12 o'clock and runs clockwise, largest slice first, with white separators between slices and no labels. Donut radius is 65-80% (legend horizontal) or 80-95%; the percentage appears in the centre on hover.
marks.notes: Gauges are a first-class family: horizontal, semicircle, circular and dial. The track (unfilled remainder) is grey.

labels.dataLabels: Not shown on bars or lines in the examples. Pie/donut use hover. Gauges show a large bold value.
labels.numberFormat: Large numbers K, M, B, T (combinable with currency, e.g. '12 K€'). Percent with a space: '20 %'. Currency uses local symbols with a space before €: '29,99 €'. Axis increments are round numbers.
labels.dates: Date DD/MM/YYYY. 12-hour '7:00 AM'. 24-hour '07:00'. Days 'Mon, Tue'. Months 'Jan, Feb'. Specific days 'day + month' (10 Jan); specific months 'Jan 2021'. Quarters Q1–Q4.
labels.notes: Skip axis labels at regular intervals rather than crowding them. Never slant labels — rotate the chart (horizontal bars) instead.

furniture.title: Titles describe the question the dataset answers and are as short as possible. An optional subtitle explains the insight. Both are sentence case.
furniture.other: Charts sit inside page content or dashboards. The guide's examples have generous white margins and no card border.

annotations: Highlight a single data point in orange (#f16e00) and render the rest in neutral grey (#666666).
layout: ODS Charts handles responsive resize and dark/light-mode switching via a theme observer. Donut centre moves to 40% when a legend is present. Horizontal gauge grid: left 20, top 32, right 20, height 32.
interaction: Tooltips (ODS Charts 'popover') can serve as legends on hover. The popover is HTML/CSS with a 10px arrow, light/dark aware, using the legend's square colour swatches. Clicking a legend item toggles its series.
accessibility: All categorical, single and sequential colours meet WCAG 2.2 AA 3:1 contrast against the primary background in light and dark mode, and are distinguishable for most colour-blind users (not for monochromacy). Legend swatches get a black or white outline. The 'Getting started' page requires an accessibility plan.

chartTypes.notes: Chart chooser groups: change over time, ranking (always sorted ascending or descending), part to whole, comparison, spatial, deviation, current status. Novice audiences get simple bars and lines.

distinctiveRules.rule: Gridlines and the gauge track are always light grey #cccccc (dark mode #666666); there are no tick marks.
distinctiveRules.quote: Within a chart or graph, grey is used for all grid lines and as the track colour. color.dataviz.gridlines #cccccc

distinctiveRules.rule: Gridlines run only along the value axis: horizontal for column and line charts, vertical for horizontal bar charts. The baseline axis line is a slightly heavier grey.
distinctiveRules.quote: Example images: vertical bars show only horizontal #ccc rules; horizontal bars show only vertical rules.

distinctiveRules.rule: Emphasis uses one orange highlight (#f16e00) against neutral grey (#666666) for everything else. Orange is not part of the categorical palette.
distinctiveRules.quote: To make the highlighted information stand out, always pair it with color.chart.neutral for less important data.

distinctiveRules.rule: Categorical colours are applied strictly in token order (tier-1 purple #5b2f98, tier-2 green #3ba06e, tier-3 magenta #b20077, tier-4 ochre #a38200, tier-5 blue #0073b2, ...).
distinctiveRules.quote: Colours should be applied in sequence as numbered in the token names.

distinctiveRules.rule: Each chart colour is a light/dark token pair. Sequential ramps invert in dark mode (low values dark, high values light).
distinctiveRules.quote: In light mode, lower values are lighter and higher values are darker. In Dark mode, lower values are darker and higher values are lighter.

distinctiveRules.rule: Y-axis labels are right-aligned and vertically centred on their gridline. X-axis labels are centred under each bar or point.
distinctiveRules.quote: Right align labels on the y-axis. Align vertically to the centre of the grid lines... Centre align labels for bar and line charts on the x-axis.

distinctiveRules.rule: Never slant axis labels. Switch to horizontal bars for long labels, and skip labels at regular intervals.
distinctiveRules.quote: Don't slant labels as it makes them difficult to read... Skip labels in regular intervals.

distinctiveRules.rule: The value axis extends one round increment beyond the data maximum.
distinctiveRules.quote: Always include an additional increment greater than the dataset.

distinctiveRules.rule: Titles and subtitles are sentence case. The title states the question; the subtitle gives the insight.
distinctiveRules.quote: Titles should describe the question the dataset is trying to represent... Always display titles and subtitles using sentence case.

distinctiveRules.rule: Legend swatches are coloured squares with a black or white outline, shown only when there is more than one colour. The default position is below the plot, left-aligned, with at most two lines.
distinctiveRules.quote: Coloured squares are used in legends... a black or white outline is used to surround each coloured square... Up to two lines of legends are displayed by default.

distinctiveRules.rule: French-style number formatting: a space before % and €, comma decimal ('29,99 €', '20 %'), and K/M/B/T abbreviations ('12 K€').
distinctiveRules.quote: Include a space between the value and the % symbol... When displaying the Euro symbol, include a space between the value and the symbol.

distinctiveRules.rule: Dates are DD/MM/YYYY. Months are abbreviated to three letters ('Jan 2021'); quarters are 'Q1'.
Pie slices start at 12 o'clock, run clockwise largest-first, are separated by white borders and carry no labels.
Ranking charts are always sorted ascending or descending.
distinctiveRules.quote: Ranking charts should always be arranged in ascending or descending order.

distinctiveRules.rule: Lines are 2px, smooth by default in ODS Charts, with no point markers unless the 'points' style is chosen.
distinctiveRules.quote: getLineChartConfiguration(config = { lineStyle: ODSChartsLineStyle.SMOOTH }); broken style: width: 2, symbolSize: 0

referenceImages.describes: Vertical bar chart, six categories A–F, all bars one violet (#8d60cd-like), flat tops, square corners, bar width about 55% of the band. Light grey horizontal gridlines at 0–50 in steps of 10; a heavier grey baseline at 0. No vertical gridlines, no tick marks, no y-axis line. Black Helvetica Neue labels: y labels right-aligned left of the plot, x labels centred under the bars. No title, legend or source; white background with large margins.

Single line chart: one deep-purple (#5b2f98) straight-segment line about 2–3px, no markers, Jan–Jun. Light grey horizontal gridlines 0–50 and a heavier grey baseline with short grey tick marks under the month labels. Black sans-serif labels, y right-aligned. No title or legend; wide white margins.

Stacked horizontal bar chart (Accounts A–D) with segments in categorical tiers 1–3: deep purple #5b2f98, green #3ba06e, magenta #b20077, separated by thin white gaps. Vertical light grey gridlines 0–100 every 10, a thicker grey y-axis line at 0, value labels centred below. Category labels right-aligned on the left. Legend below the plot, left-aligned with the plot edge: small solid square swatches followed by 'Dataset 1/2/3' in black regular type on one row.

Pie with five slices starting at 12 o'clock, clockwise and largest first: purple #5b2f98, green #3ba06e, magenta #b20077, ochre #a38200, blue #0073b2. Thin white borders between slices; no labels, legend or title.

'Do' example: horizontal bar chart with long category names ('Information technology', 'Communication services') right-aligned in black to the left of the bars, so labels stay horizontal. Single violet colour, vertical grey gridlines 0–60, heavier grey zero line on the left, x-axis numbers centred beneath.
